question.prompt: Let \(S\) be the set of points \((x,y)\) in the coordinate plane such that two of the three quantities \(3,\) \(x+2,\) and \(y-4\) are equal and the third of the three quantities is no greater than this common value. Which of the following is a correct description of \(S?\)

choices.content:
three lines whose pairwise intersections are three distinct
points
three rays with a common endpoint

solutions.title: Examine the three equal pairs
solutions.explanation:
The equal quantities must be at least as large as the remaining quantity. There are three possible pairs to examine.

1. If \(3=x+2\ge y-4\), then
\[
x=1,\qquad y\le7.
\]
These points form the ray starting at \((1,7)\) and extending downward.

2. If \(3=y-4\ge x+2\), then
\[
y=7,\qquad x\le1.
\]
These points form the ray starting at \((1,7)\) and extending leftward.

3. If \(x+2=y-4\ge3\), then
\[
y=x+6,\qquad x\ge1.
\]
These points form the ray starting at \((1,7)\) and extending upward and to the right.

Every allowed point falls into at least one of these cases, and every point on these rays satisfies the original condition. The rays meet only at \((1,7)\), where all three quantities equal \(3\).

Thus \(\boxed{S\text{ consists of three rays with a common endpoint}}\), choice \(\text{E}\).
